summary: A lighthouse has stood on Point Gratiot on Lake Erie since the 1820s; the 1870s tower, with its 1857 third-order Fresnel lens, and keeper's house are now a veterans' museum.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The station was established 1827 per USLHS; the first tower was completed in 1826 per LighthouseFriends. The present tower: 1 July 1876 per LighthouseFriends and USLHS, 1875 in Rowlett and in the record.

notes_for_editor: Corpus holds Light-House Board reports only from 1891; the 1868 and 1874 reports are quoted at second hand through LighthouseFriends. Newspaper searches (Dean Richmond, 1893) were attempted but loc.gov was slow and returned nothing usable in time, so wreck stories rest on LighthouseFriends. NRHP nominations are not digitised. Disagreements flagged in text: first-lit date (1875 vs 1876), tower material (limestone vs rubblestone-in-brick), pierhead storm date (31 Dec vs 12 Dec 1895 within one report volume), automation date (1960 in the record vs 1961 roster end vs c1962), Taggert resigning 1885 yet rostered to 1887. The 1928 Bulletin item names only 'F. D. Arnold, keeper' and gives 23 July; year of the rescue itself is assumed 1928 volume. LighthouseFriends roster matches the USLHS roster line for line. Light height: the record has 25 m, USLHS 82 ft.
